raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Summary

  Building on #7277, this change adds `expert_num_distributed_optimizer_instances` so dense and expert parameters can use independent instance counts.

  - Defaults to `num_distributed_optimizer_instances`, preserving existing behavior.
  - Reuses outer process groups when instance counts match.

> Are you sure it's needed? This changes the mesh and the mesh is typically aligned with network topology -- most likely `[inter-nvl, intra-nvl]` for production settings.

Oh, maybe this is for supporting something like HFSDP for dense and Zero3+EP for MoE? That would make sense to me.

> > Are you sure it's needed? This changes the mesh and the mesh is typically aligned with network topology -- most likely `[inter-nvl, intra-nvl]` for production settings.
> 
> Oh, maybe this is for supporting something like HFSDP for dense and Zero3+EP for MoE? That would make sense to me.

Yes, I recently found that some customers require using HSDP, with the outer dimension set to ZeRO-1 and the inner dimension set to ZeRO-3 for dense part, while using a fully ZeRO-1 configuration plus EP for MoE part.

Alternatively, we could add a single switch to control whether HSDP is enabled for the expert, for example: --enable-expert-hsdp 🤔
cc @wujingyue for the earlier discussion about the HSDP integration .

> the outer dimension set to ZeRO-1 and the inner dimension set to ZeRO-3 for dense part, while using a fully ZeRO-1 configuration plus EP for MoE part.

This use case makes sense to me. 

> Alternatively, we could add a single switch to control whether HSDP is enabled for the expert, for example: --enable-expert-hsdp

I'm not sure about the best API.

Could you rebase the PR so I can review it again? 

In general, we've been using DataParallelConfig as a domain-specific language to dictate how to fully_shard. However, the friction has always been that DataParallelConfig is less powerful. 

Have you considered letting users (instead of the mcore adapter) fully_shard directly and still running that model in Megatron's training loop? That could be the right solution going forward.

> > the outer dimension set to ZeRO-1 and the inner dimension set to ZeRO-3 for dense part, while using a fully ZeRO-1 configuration plus EP for MoE part.
> 
> This use case makes sense to me.
> 
> > Alternatively, we could add a single switch to control whether HSDP is enabled for the expert, for example: --enable-expert-hsdp
> 
> I'm not sure about the best API.
> 
> Could you rebase the PR so I can review it again?
> 
> In general, we've been using DataParallelConfig as a domain-specific language to dictate how to fully_shard. However, the friction has always been that DataParallelConfig is less powerful.
> 
> Have you considered letting users (instead of the mcore adapter) fully_shard directly and still running that model in Megatron's training loop? That could be the right solution going forward.

That sounds useful for advanced users, but I think most users still want MCore to handle the sharding setup. I’d keep the config-based path and offer direct fully_shard for cases that need more control.

> Reuses outer process groups when instance counts match.

Even when instance counts match, there can be benefits to having separate groups. For example, my example in https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8519 would be supported by Mcore, rather than a failure. (In the context of https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8519, the example was just meant to illustrate a gap in the argument validation logic.)

I think this PR is an improvement so I don't want to block it. But I would like to extend it further in the future.

> Are you sure it's needed? This changes the mesh and the mesh is typically aligned with network topology -- most likely `[inter-nvl, intra-nvl]` for production settings.

Oh, maybe this is for supporting something like HFSDP for dense and Zero3+EP for MoE? That would make sense to me.

> > Are you sure it's needed? This changes the mesh and the mesh is typically aligned with network topology -- most likely `[inter-nvl, intra-nvl]` for production settings.
> 
> Oh, maybe this is for supporting something like HFSDP for dense and Zero3+EP for MoE? That would make sense to me.

Yes, I recently found that some customers require using HSDP, with the outer dimension set to ZeRO-1 and the inner dimension set to ZeRO-3 for dense part, while using a fully ZeRO-1 configuration plus EP for MoE part.

Alternatively, we could add a single switch to control whether HSDP is enabled for the expert, for example: --enable-expert-hsdp 🤔
cc @wujingyue for the earlier discussion about the HSDP integration .

> the outer dimension set to ZeRO-1 and the inner dimension set to ZeRO-3 for dense part, while using a fully ZeRO-1 configuration plus EP for MoE part.

This use case makes sense to me. 

> Alternatively, we could add a single switch to control whether HSDP is enabled for the expert, for example: --enable-expert-hsdp

I'm not sure about the best API.

Could you rebase the PR so I can review it again? 

In general, we've been using DataParallelConfig as a domain-specific language to dictate how to fully_shard. However, the friction has always been that DataParallelConfig is less powerful. 

Have you considered letting users (instead of the mcore adapter) fully_shard directly and still running that model in Megatron's training loop? That could be the right solution going forward.

> > the outer dimension set to ZeRO-1 and the inner dimension set to ZeRO-3 for dense part, while using a fully ZeRO-1 configuration plus EP for MoE part.
> 
> This use case makes sense to me.
> 
> > Alternatively, we could add a single switch to control whether HSDP is enabled for the expert, for example: --enable-expert-hsdp
> 
> I'm not sure about the best API.
> 
> Could you rebase the PR so I can review it again?
> 
> In general, we've been using DataParallelConfig as a domain-specific language to dictate how to fully_shard. However, the friction has always been that DataParallelConfig is less powerful.
> 
> Have you considered letting users (instead of the mcore adapter) fully_shard directly and still running that model in Megatron's training loop? That could be the right solution going forward.

That sounds useful for advanced users, but I think most users still want MCore to handle the sharding setup. I’d keep the config-based path and offer direct fully_shard for cases that need more control.

> Reuses outer process groups when instance counts match.

Even when instance counts match, there can be benefits to having separate groups. For example, my example in https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8519 would be supported by Mcore, rather than a failure. (In the context of https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/pull/8519, the example was just meant to illustrate a gap in the argument validation logic.)

I think this PR is an improvement so I don't want to block it. But I would like to extend it further in the future.
